scenarios.name: Scan-to-Receive QR / Collect Request
scenarios.example: A stranger asked me to scan a QR code to receive money and enter my PIN.
redFlags: A PIN is asked 'to receive' money
QR or collect request from a stranger
Money is said to be 'coming to you'
scenarios.why: Entering your UPI PIN always SENDS money. You never need a PIN, or a QR scan, to receive money.
actions: Do not scan or approve it, and never enter your PIN
Decline the collect request and block the sender
If money already left, call 1930 immediately and report at cybercrime.gov.in
scenarios.source: RBI BE(A)WARE booklet; NPCI UPI safety awareness

question.text: Did the app or QR ask you to enter your UPI PIN?
question.yes: they asked me to enter my pin to receive money
question.no: they did not ask for my pin

scenarios.name: Fake Refund / Cashback Trap
scenarios.example: I got a message saying my refund failed and I should click a link to claim it.
redFlags: Refund for something you don't remember buying
A link or QR is needed to 'claim' it
Message from an unknown sender
scenarios.why: Real refunds are credited automatically to your account. Nobody needs a link, QR or PIN to give you your own refund.
actions: Don't tap the link or scan the QR
Delete the message and block the number
Check the real order status only in the official shopping or bank app

question.text: Did the message come with a link, QR or ask for your PIN?
question.yes: it has a link and asks me to enter my pin to claim
question.no: no link and no pin was asked

scenarios.name: Fake Bank / KYC Call
scenarios.example: Someone from the 'bank' called saying my KYC will expire today and asked for my OTP.
redFlags: Caller says KYC or account will be blocked
Asks for OTP, PIN or card details
Creates urgency and fear
scenarios.why: Banks and NPCI never ask for your OTP, PIN or CVV on a call. The OTP is the key that lets the scammer take your money.
actions: Hang up without sharing anything
Call your bank on the number printed on your card or in its official app
If you shared an OTP, call your bank and 1930 right now
scenarios.source: RBI BE(A)WARE booklet; NPCI UPI safety awareness

question.text: Did they ask you for an OTP, PIN or card details?
question.yes: they asked me to share my otp
question.no: they did not ask for any otp or pin

scenarios.name: Screen-Share App Scam (AnyDesk / TeamViewer)
scenarios.example: A 'support agent' asked me to install AnyDesk to fix my payment problem.
redFlags: Asked to install a remote-access app
Support call you did not start
They want you to open your payment app
scenarios.why: Remote apps let the scammer see your screen, read your OTPs and move money from your phone directly.
actions: Do not install it, or uninstall it right away if you already did
Turn off internet, then call your bank to block UPI/cards
Report to 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in

question.text: Did they ask you to install an app or share your screen?
question.yes: they asked me to install anydesk and share my screen
question.no: they did not ask me to install anything

scenarios.name: Fake Buyer / Seller Advance Scam
scenarios.example: A buyer on OLX said he will pay me and sent a request; a seller wants an advance before delivery.
redFlags: Insists on advance or 'token' payment
Buyer sends a request you must 'approve' to get paid
Wants to move chat to WhatsApp quickly, no meeting
scenarios.why: Real buyers only need your UPI ID to pay you. If you must approve or enter a PIN, money is going OUT. Advance to strangers often vanishes.
actions: Never approve a collect request from a buyer
Meet in public and pay only on delivery or after you see the product
Block and report the listing on the platform
scenarios.source: RBI BE(A)WARE booklet; police cyber cell advisories

question.text: Are they asking you to pay in advance, or to approve a request to get paid?
question.yes: they want an advance payment and a request to approve
question.no: no advance and no approval needed

scenarios.name: 'Sent by Mistake, Please Return' Trick
scenarios.example: A stranger sent ₹5,000 by mistake and is calling me to send it back.
redFlags: Unknown person sends money 'by mistake'
Pressure to return it quickly, to another account/UPI ID
Emotional story (emergency, medical)
scenarios.why: The incoming money can be from a fraud or stolen account, and may be reversed later, while your 'return' is real money out of your pocket.
actions: Don't send money back to a different UPI ID or number
Tell your bank and let them handle any real mistaken credit
Don't spend the money. Report to 1930 if you are being pressured
scenarios.source: Police cyber cell advisories; RBI BE(A)WARE booklet

question.text: Did the person ask you to return the money straight to them, outside the bank?
question.yes: they want me to send it back directly to their number
question.no: i have not been asked to send anything

scenarios.name: Fake Customer Care Number
scenarios.example: I searched Google for the customer care number of an app and they asked for my card details.
redFlags: Number found through search results, ads or social posts
Agent asks for OTP, PIN or to install an app
Agent contacts you first after you posted a complaint
scenarios.why: Scammers publish fake helpline numbers and watch social media complaints. Real support never asks for your PIN or OTP.
actions: Use only the helpline inside the official app or on the official website/card
Hang up if they ask for PIN, OTP or to install anything
Report the number at cybercrime.gov.in

question.text: Did you find this number through a web search or social media?
question.yes: i found the number by searching online
question.no: the number is from the official app or my card

scenarios.name: Lottery, Prize or KBC-style Win
scenarios.example: I got a message that I won a lottery and must pay a small fee to receive the prize.
redFlags: You never entered any contest
You must pay a 'fee', 'tax' or 'courier' charge first
Winner message from a random number
scenarios.why: Genuine prizes never ask you to pay money first. The 'small fee' is the whole scam, and it is usually followed by more demands.
actions: Ignore and do not pay any fee
Block the number and delete the message
Report on cybercrime.gov.in if you lost money

question.text: Are they asking you to pay a fee or tax before you get the prize?
question.yes: they want a fee first to release the prize
question.no: no payment is needed from me

scenarios.name: Part-Time Job / 'Task' Scam
scenarios.example: A Telegram group offers money for liking videos but now asks me to deposit money to unlock tasks.
redFlags: High pay for very easy online work
You must deposit money to 'unlock' tasks or withdraw
Contact only via WhatsApp or Telegram groups
scenarios.why: They pay a small amount at first to build trust, then demand larger and larger deposits. Money you 'earn' can never be withdrawn.
actions: Stop paying, since nothing will be returned
Save chats and payment proofs
Call 1930 and file a report on cybercrime.gov.in quickly
scenarios.source: Police cyber cell advisories; cybercrime.gov.in awareness

question.text: Are you being asked to deposit money to earn or withdraw?
question.yes: they asked me to deposit money to unlock tasks
question.no: i am not asked to pay anything

scenarios.name: 'Electricity Will Be Cut Tonight' SMS
scenarios.example: An SMS said my electricity will be disconnected tonight unless I call an officer and pay.
redFlags: Threat of disconnection tonight
Asks you to call a personal mobile number
Asks you to pay a small bill via a link or install an app
scenarios.why: Electricity boards do not disconnect connections through random SMS from personal numbers. The 'officer' will try to take over your phone or payments.
actions: Do not call or click
Check the bill in the official board app or website
Report the number to 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in
scenarios.source: Electricity board and police cyber cell advisories

question.text: Does the message ask you to call a mobile number or install an app?
question.yes: it asks me to call a number and install an app
question.no: it only shows my bill and nothing else

scenarios.name: Fake Payment Screenshot
scenarios.example: A customer showed me a payment success screenshot but I did not get an SMS or sound.
redFlags: Customer shows a screenshot instead of waiting
No bank SMS and no soundbox confirmation
Customer is in a hurry to leave
scenarios.why: Screenshots and edited payment apps are easy to fake. Only your own bank credit confirms that money has arrived.
actions: Check your own bank or UPI app for the credit before giving the goods
Ask the customer to wait or pay again
Report repeated cases to local police
scenarios.source: RBI BE(A)WARE booklet; NPCI merchant awareness

question.text: Have you seen the amount credited in YOUR own app or bank SMS?
question.yes: i saw the credit in my own app
question.no: i have not seen the credit in my own account

scenarios.name: Instant Loan App / Processing Fee
scenarios.example: An app promised an instant loan but asked for a processing fee and access to my contacts.
redFlags: Loan approved without checks, fee asked first
App asks for contacts, photos and SMS access
Threats or shaming messages to your contacts
scenarios.why: Illegal loan apps charge upfront fees, steal data and harass borrowers. Genuine lenders are registered with the RBI.
actions: Do not pay the fee or share more data
Uninstall the app and report it
Borrow only from RBI-registered banks and NBFCs, and report threats to 1930
scenarios.source: RBI digital lending warnings; cybercrime.gov.in advisories

question.text: Did they ask for a fee, or for access to your contacts?
question.yes: they asked for a processing fee and my contacts
question.no: they asked for nothing like that

scenarios.name: 'Friend or Relative in Emergency' Message
scenarios.example: A new number says it is my cousin who lost his phone and needs money urgently.
redFlags: 'Hi, this is my new number', no proof of identity
Emergency (accident, hospital, lost wallet)
Asks you not to call, payment to a new account
scenarios.why: Scammers copy photos and names from social media to pretend to be someone you trust and rush you into paying.
actions: Call the real person on their old, saved number first
Ask a question only the real person would know
Do not pay until you have confirmed, and report the number
scenarios.source: Police cyber cell advisories; cybercrime.gov.in awareness

question.text: Have you spoken to this person on their old, saved number?
question.yes: i called their old number and they confirmed
question.no: i have not been able to confirm on their old number

scenarios.name: 'I Sent My Code to Your Number by Mistake'
scenarios.example: A person says they sent a 6-digit code to my number by mistake and wants me to forward it.
redFlags: Asks you to forward a verification code
Message appears to come from a friend or stranger
Urgent, polite tone, 'please help'
scenarios.why: That code is the lock on THEIR new account attempt: your number is being used to take over a WhatsApp or UPI account or to register the scammer's device.
actions: Never forward any verification code to anyone
Turn on two-step verification in WhatsApp
Block the sender and tell your contacts if your account was hijacked

question.text: Did you forward or read out the code to them?
question.yes: i already shared the code with them
question.no: i did not share the code

scenarios.name: Fake APK / 'Update' File (Challan, KYC, Scheme)
scenarios.example: I got a WhatsApp file called RTO_Challan.apk and a message to install it or pay a fine.
redFlags: A file ending in .apk sent over chat or SMS
Threat: challan, KYC, electricity or government-scheme update
Asks you to allow 'install from unknown sources'
scenarios.why: These files install spyware that reads your SMS, OTPs and UPI app. No government or bank sends apps over chat.
actions: Do not open or install it, and delete the file
If installed, switch to airplane mode, uninstall it and call your bank at once
Report to 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in

question.text: Is it an .apk or an app that you were told to install outside the Play Store?
question.yes: it is an apk file i was told to install
question.no: it is not an app, only a normal message

scenarios.name: 'Digital Arrest' / Fake Police or Courier Parcel Call
scenarios.example: A video caller in police uniform said a parcel in my name has drugs and I must stay on call and pay to avoid arrest.
redFlags: Caller claims to be police, CBI, customs or courier about a parcel
Tells you to stay on the video call and not tell anyone
Demands money to 'verify' or avoid arrest
scenarios.why: There is no such thing as a 'digital arrest' in Indian law. Police and agencies never arrest people on video call or ask for money to clear a case.
actions: Disconnect, and do not transfer any money
Talk to family and call your local police station or 1930
Report on cybercrime.gov.in
scenarios.source: MHA I4C and PIB advisories; cybercrime.gov.in

question.text: Are they telling you to stay on the call, keep it secret, or pay money?
question.yes: they told me to stay on the call and not tell anyone and pay money
question.no: they are not asking me to pay or stay on the call
